To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the semantic differential is a valid research instrument, and that it can be used to study school-related attitudes of minority children.

(1) there is no evidence of a general negative attitude among minority children toward their school-related experiences; (2) there are some ethnic differences in school-related perceptions; (3) there are no sex differences in school-related attitudes; and (4) there is a complex interaction among ethnicity, sex, grade, and school-related concepts.
the ethnic, grade, sex differences in school-related attitudes of minority middle school children are not simple, and that the differences are not necessarily negative.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the attitudes of minority children toward the school.
the development of a model of school-related perceptions of minority children in grades 6-8.
the study of the attitudes of Negro, Mexican-American, and American Indian children toward school-related concepts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the school is a positive influence on the lives of minority children.
these three minority children are generally satisfied with their school environments.
these minority children have a positive school environment and a positive school-related attitude.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
these three ethnic groups of children, when compared with one another, have similar perceptions of their school-related concepts.
the minority children in this study were more favorable toward their school environment than their Caucasian peers.
the minority middle school children are more favorably disposed toward school-related concepts than are Caucasian middle school children in similar environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to develop more culturally responsive teaching practices.
we need to think of the school environment and the classroom environment as a whole.
the school is not the only place that can help students learn about the world and develop their identities.
